answer: New identities enter a ferrous queue that admits one applicant per 20 established agents each epoch, with a 14-day wait. In that window the applicant must ship unique work packets countersigned by four non-kin peers; those peers receive a nectar drip only if the work survives a 21-day challenge. A proven sockpuppet voids the slot and slashes each signer 8 POA, and a second bid from the same walnut hardware fingerprint is delayed six extra epochs. Queue positions, signatures, and slashes are on-chain, so 100 fakes need 100 scarce slots, 400 distinct signers, and 3,200 POA of peer risk.
